WITHDRAWN CONCLUSION, 2026-09-14: see docs/CLAIMS-AUDIT.md and the fix.cvt_chan_count_programmed gate. The read procedure behind 'cannot be reached over the codec's I2C master' returned the same value for a populated and an empty I2C address, so that half was never shown. The measurement below is real and is kept; only the amplifier conclusion is withdrawn. ISOLATED, 2026-09-14. A self-verifying triage shows headphones AUDIBLE after a resume through the same hw:0,0 4-channel stream, while the speakers are silent with playback confirmed OK. Controller, DMA, codec, analog path and driver logic are therefore all working; the fault is only in converter 0x0a -> pin 0x1d -> TDM -> the four TAS5758L amplifiers, which lose their configuration when their supply drops and cannot be reached over the codec's I2C master. Not fixable from the driver with current knowledge.

WITHDRAWN 20260914.04. The finding was 'amp addresses answer identically to address 0x20, therefore the amplifiers are not reachable'. That is an uncalibrated instrument reporting on itself: the identical answer appeared in the WORKING state, where the amplifiers are known to be alive, so the procedure cannot distinguish a present device from an absent one and has measured neither. IDENTIFIED AND FIXED 2026-09-15, reproduced on the test machine within the hour the maintainer reported it. The stock ACP path analog-output-speaker declares '[Jack Headphone] state.plugged = no'. This card's only analog output mapping (analog-surround-40, the one configuration the PCM accepts) has exactly that single port, and the driver serves headphones through it by switching converters itself. A plugged jack therefore made the port unavailable, the profile with it, and WirePlumber selected input:analog-stereo - a card with no sink, shown as 'Schein-Ausgabe'/Dummy Output, silent on speakers and headphones alike. Surfaced 84 s after the resume at 20:50:57 because profile selection reruns there. api.acp.auto-profile/auto-port = false were necessary but never sufficient: they stop a switch, not the profile going unavailable.

RESOLVED 2026-09-14: the header no longer claims 'no writes of any kind'; it now states exactly what is written (128 SET_COEF_INDEX coefficient-selector writes on widget 0x24, no data register writes) and points to macbook91-codec-state as the capability-gated successor for new work. The remaining substantive criticisms are known limitations of a superseded tool, not an open defect: 1209 is a count of printed fields, not of independent valid hardware reads; it duplicates pin_sense; it has no capability-derived register map; it reads no amplifier register; it skips some OSError and can mask a None.

AppleHDATDMAmpTAS5758L::init ends with this->enable(true) at 0xa2e126 (vptr+0x1a8 -> 0xa2e1b4). macOS programs the amplifiers itself, once, when setupTDMDevices builds the TDM device list; AppleHDAPath::enable never calls that slot, so it is not per stream. 'Mac firmware programs them at power-on' is contradicted for the programming step.

TAS5758L has neither performPowerRailSave nor performPowerRailRestore; TAS5764L has both, as do AppleHDAWidgetCS4208, AppleHDAFunctionGroupCS8409 and AppleHDATDM_CS42L83. macOS does nothing to reprogram these amplifiers after a sleep. Either their configuration survives - which would make the resume fault codec- or TDM-side - or something outside AppleHDA re-establishes it. See CLAIMS-AUDIT.md D6.

layout 127 and 129 are NOT wholly identical to 121, as previously recorded; only their TDMDevices and DFET control blocks are. The amplifier topology claim holds whichever layout MacBook9,1 selects. Decoded copies are kept outside this repository.

FIXED. macbook91-amp-transport read AC_PAR_VENDOR_ID from the audio function group; it lives on the root node 0x00, so the AFG answered 0 and the probe declared a CS4208 not to be a CS4208. Both privileged runs either side of a suspend were lost at that gate. The AFG is now discovered from NODE_COUNT/FUNCTION_TYPE and the state is recorded before any verdict.

tools/macbook91-codec-state: node list from the codec's own NODE_COUNT, every field gated on the widget's advertised capability, '<unsupported>' / '<error N>' / '<no-response>' all distinct from 0, coefficient index saved and restored, and it does not claim to be read-only. diff labels volatile fields. RUN 2026-09-14 12:55 UTC. Cold boot with speakers AUDIBLE, then one deep suspend, both captured with macbook91-codec-state: 35 nodes, 582 fields, 0 read errors each. EXACTLY ONE functional field differs: subsystem_id_verb 106b6500 -> 10134208. The 128 coefficients, all 19 pin configuration defaults, every pin control, every amplifier gain/mute, every power state, every stream format and GPIO 0x07/0x37/0x31 are all byte-identical. CAVEAT: taken at rest, with every widget in D3. Repeat with probe --with-stream.

MEASURED: verb 0xF20 on the AFG returns 0x106b6500 at cold boot and 0x10134208 after a deep resume - the same degradation a PCI re-probe causes. The subsystem id register is firmware-programmed state that the suspend destroys, and it is the ONLY readable firmware-owned register the driver does not restore. Diagnostically it is the fingerprint of a codec reset; it is not expected to affect audio, and must not be 'fixed' as though it would.

FIXED. macbook91-codec-state had a fixed verb list after all and omitted STRIPE_CONTROL (0xf24), which converters 0x02 and 0x0a both advertise and which the vendored macOS trace reads on seven converters expecting 0x00100000. Added with CVT_CHAN_COUNT, SDI_SELECT and the per-widget PCM capability. The 582-field comparison above predates this and did not cover them.

RUN 2026-09-14 13:09/13:10 UTC. Cold boot, speakers audible (maintainer-confirmed); one deep suspend; speakers silent (maintainer-confirmed). 722 capability-validated fields either side, at rest AND with a 4-channel stream of digital silence running. Result: converter 0x0a cvt_chan_count 0x03 -> 0x00 in both comparisons. That is the defect. subsystem_id_verb also degrades, but it is identity, not function. Caveat found 2026-10-15: that capture read every amplifier gain/mute field as input amplifier, right channel, index 0, so amplifier output state was not compared. tools/macbook91-codec-state addresses them correctly since then (unreleased); no new capture was made.

THE DEFECT, measured: converter 0x0a's channel count register holds channels-1 and goes 0x03 -> 0x00 across a suspend, so the converter emits one channel into a four-slot TDM frame while the format word still reads 0x4013. Not restored by anything: regmap.c:132 excludes AC_VERB_GET_CVT_CHAN_COUNT from the writeable set ('managed in HDMI CA code') so regmap_sync never replays it, and the vendored macOS trace never writes it. Converter 0x02 has no such field, which is why headphones always worked.

CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE by the maintainer, 2026-09-14: with the channel-count fix installed, sound from the internal speakers both before and after a deep suspend, repeatedly, where every earlier release was silent after the first resume. The kernel log carries 'converter 0x0a channel count 4' on each resume. NOT a full acceptance: the formal protocol is three consecutive cycles with a long S3 among them, and every S3 measured so far lasted seconds because of the lid wake - see hw.long_suspend_coverage.

The S3 path runs in full - 'Preparing to enter system sleep state S3', NVS saved, non-boot CPUs offlined, 'Waking up from system sleep state S3' - and /sys/power/suspend_stats reports success 2 with every failure counter 0. The codec loses its subsystem id, channel count and pin 0x1d across it, which only happens when it is actually powered down. The audio comparisons were taken across genuine S3 cycles.

RESOLVED 2026-09-14. LID0 is the wake source. With it disarmed (round 3) and with the maintainer's sleep hook moved into /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/ where systemd actually reads it (round 4), gpe6F did not fire at all - it had fired exactly once in every earlier suspend - and the 3-4 s wake stopped. The two rounds lasted 21.9 s and 24.4 s, which is consistent with the maintainer waking the machine by hand; the probe cannot tell that from a spurious wake, so the durations are NOT the evidence. The evidence is gpe6F falling silent. Not caused by this package: the channel-count fix behaves exactly as the build before it did.

tools/macbook91-wake-probe: snapshots every GPE counter, every per-device power/wakeup_* counter, /proc/acpi/wakeup, pm_wakeup_irq and suspend_stats; detects resume from CLOCK_BOOTTIME minus CLOCK_MONOTONIC rather than from a log or a blanked screen; reports a suspend that never happened as NONE, never as success. Fixture-tested for the 4 s, 900 s and 0 s cases.

macbook91-runner wake --disarm records the prior state of every name before touching it, toggles only the ones that differ (/proc/acpi/wakeup is a toggle, so an unconditional write to an already-disabled device ENABLES it), restores the exact prior state from the exit trap, verifies the restore and prints manual recovery if it fails.

MEASURED 2026-09-15 and maintainer-confirmed. Five deep suspends that day, from the journal, not from a probe: 06:19:42->08:03:39 (1 h 44 min), 10:03:41->10:51:53 (48 min), 13:25:40->13:48:55 (23 min), 18:25:15->18:53:57 (29 min), 19:26:33->20:50:57 (1 h 24 min), each 'PM: suspend entry (deep)'. Every resume carries 'A1534: restored 128 coefficients, 19 pin configs, digi 0x111, converter 0x0a channel count 4'. The maintainer confirms sound after them. This supersedes the earlier concern that only seconds-long S3 had ever been seen. TWO LIMITS, both real: these ran under the channel-count fix of 2026-09-14, and the headphone fix of 2026-09-15 changed no driver source at all, so the cvt_chan_count restore under test is byte-identical; and the 20:50:57 resume did leave the machine silent - for the unrelated userspace reason the headphone fix addresses (rootcause.acp_port_jack_coupling), not because the codec restore failed. Its restore line is present like all the others.

macbook91-wake-probe prw decodes the _PRW packages out of the DSDT's raw AML - NameOp, _PRW, PackageOp, PkgLength, element count, BytePrefix/ZeroOp/OneOp/WordPrefix - because iasl is not installed and the table is root-only. The encoding is verified against synthetic bytes by the test suite before it ever touches the real table. The device match is positional against /proc/acpi/wakeup, which is a heuristic, is offered only when the counts agree, and says so in its own output.

/etc/systemd/system-sleep/legacy-hook-sleep_hacks is executable and was installed to stop the lid waking the machine, and it has NEVER run: journalctl -t SLEEPHACK has no entries in any boot on record while /usr/bin/logger exists. systemd reads ONLY /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/ - that is the only such path in the systemd-sleep binary and the only one systemd-sleep(8) documents. Positive control: /var/log/sa/sa14 was written at 18:16:36, the exact second of a resume, by sysstat.sleep from /usr/lib. Fix: install the script into /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/ and remove the /etc copy - exactly one copy, because /proc/acpi/wakeup is a toggle and two scripts cancel out. FIXED by the maintainer: the script now lives in /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/ and the probe confirms runs=True.

MISS FIXED. The first investigation checked sleep.conf and logind.conf and never looked at the sleep-hook directories. macbook91-wake-probe now records both, flags a hook that rewrites /proc/acpi/wakeup in the directory systemd really reads (it would change the armed set between the snapshot and the suspend), and flags an executable in a directory systemd does not read as never running. Three tests, one of which re-checks the systemd-sleep binary rather than trusting the write-up.
